sources.title: 1853 Constitution with dated amendments
sources.usage: Read historical primary compilation Articles 1,35–36,74: federal republic, historic names, bicameral Congress and President. Later 1957 amendment explicitly marked and excluded from earlier facts; formal core does not establish unrestricted democracy.

sources.title: Nicolás Avellaneda presidential period
sources.usage: Term 12 October 1874–12 October 1880; covers full 1878 and first part of 1880.

sources.title: Roca first presidential period
sources.usage: Term 12 October 1880–12 October 1886; handover corroborates Avellaneda end.

sources.title: Yrigoyen second presidential period
sources.usage: Term 12 October 1928–6 September 1930, ended by overthrow.

sources.title: Justo presidential period
sources.usage: 20 February 1932–20 February 1938; only term used; erroneous death entry excluded.

sources.title: Ortiz presidential period
sources.usage: Body begins 20 February 1938, despite erroneous 1939 heading; corroborated by Chamber inauguration index. Later death/resignation confusion not imported.

sources.title: Chamber presidential messages index
sources.usage: Ortiz inauguration explicitly 20 February 1938; Frondizi inauguration 1 May 1958 and 1960 legislative message listed.

sources.title: Farrell de facto presidency
sources.usage: De facto President; source term 25 February 1944–4 June 1946 covers entire 1945. 1944 start discrepancy immaterial to bounded 1945 claims.

sources.title: Museo Histórico Sarmiento: federal capital history
sources.usage: Executive and Legislature moved temporarily to Belgrano during Tejedor revolt; Buenos Aires declared Federal Capital by law on 20 September 1880. Temporary seat interval unprovided.

sources.title: 17 October 1945 mobilization
sources.usage: 17 October 1945 worker mobilization in Plaza de Mayo obtained release of Juan Domingo Perón, detained days before. This does not make him President in 1945.

sources.title: Plan Conintes: represión política y sindical
sources.usage: 13 March 1960 decree 2628 publicly executed CONINTES and subordinated provincial police to military commands; 15 March decree 2639 followed. March legislative elections held with Peronism and Communist Party proscribed.
